Exports to China rose from 19% to 46% of copper exports between 2007 and 2008 (reported by MEX to UN Comtrade).

Exports to the United States rose from 19% to 42% of copper exports between 2010 and 2011 (reported by MEX to UN Comtrade).

Exports to the United States fell from 92% to 70% of gold exports between 2021 and 2022 (reported by MEX to UN Comtrade).
Exports to the United States rose from 67% to 89% of gold exports between 2024 and 2025 (reported by MEX to UN Comtrade).

sentences.text: In 2024, the influence index stands at 43.2 for China (band 36.0–68.5, from 3 of six components) and 37.6 for the United States (band 33.0–72.8, from 4 of six components). The net lean is +5.6 points toward China.
Over the five years to 2024, the index for China rose by 11.3 points and the index for the United States rose by 3.3 points.

The value for China rests on trade export share, trade import share and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.

The value for the United States rests on trade export share, trade import share, finance flow and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.
In 2025, 38% of Mexico's mineral exports (UN Comtrade value US$11.3 bn) went to China and 54% to the United States; together 92%, the rest to other destinations.
Since 2020 the share going to China rose by 3.6 points and the share going to the United States was broadly flat.
Relative to the 20-country export basket, its exports are specialised in silver (RCA 7.7), rare earths (RCA 4.9) and zinc (RCA 4.5).

11 sudden shifts in export shares are flagged from the customs data, the latest in 2025: Exports to the United States rose from 67% to 89% of gold exports between 2024 and 2025 (reported by MEX to UN Comtrade).

sentences.text: The AidData records show US$3.1 bn of documented commitments from Chinese institutions to Mexico over 2004–2021 (36 events; the source ends in 2021).
The DFC and EXIM records show US$5.2 bn of documented commitments from US institutions to Mexico over 2006–2026 (3078 events).

The lenders with the largest recorded commitments to named recipients here are Export-Import Bank of the United States (US$3.7 bn), China Development Bank (CDB) (US$1.1 bn) and US International Development Finance Corporation (US$828 m).

sentences.text: In the UN General Assembly, voting agreement in 2024 was 75% with China and 43% with the United States.
Since 2019, agreement with China fell by 7.1 points and agreement with the United States rose by 15.2 points.
Too few mineral-related legislative records naming either actor have been scored for a stance series (five per year are needed); the text model is zero-shot baseline, not yet validated.

After Executive Order 13817: A Federal Strategy to Ensure Secure and Reliable Supplies of Critical Minerals (2017-12), the share of exports to the United States moved -15.0 points (68% before, 53% after); placebo p 0.05 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After Executive Order 13817: A Federal Strategy to Ensure Secure and Reliable Supplies of Critical Minerals (2017-12), the share of exports to China moved +12.9 points (20% before, 33% after); placebo p 0.05 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: export controls on antimony items in force (Announcement 2024 No. 33 of 15 August 2024) (2024-09), the share of exports to the United States moved +10.3 points (43% before, 54% after); placebo p 0.27 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to China in 2030 is 48% (90% band 38%–58%), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 13% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to the United States in 2030 is 54% (90% band 30%–80%), from naive persistence, because no model beat it in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.

The published forecast for the influence index of China in 2030 is 45.4 (90% band 36.8–58.0), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 1% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

The published forecast for the influence index of the United States in 2030 is 37.6 (90% band 20.9–53.5), from damped local linear trend (Kalman filter, maximum likelihood), which beat naive persistence by 2% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.
Under the stated scenarios the 2030 median share to China ranges from 38% (US sourcing rules bite) to 58% (accelerated China pull); these are what-ifs with a fixed yearly shift, not predictions.

In 2025, unavailable components: legislative stance (no scored legislative records naming the actor); debt stock (no source for debt owed to the United States); finance flow (source coverage ends 2021); debt stock and diplomatic alignment (source coverage ends 2024).

Source coverage ends at different years: Chinese official finance to 2021, US finance to 2026, debt by creditor to 2024, UN votes to 2024 and trade to 2025; components beyond a source's coverage are unavailable, not zero.
12 of the dated events used above are still in the draft event list awaiting the project owner's review.
Stance values come from the text model (zero-shot baseline, not yet validated); the rest of this brief rests on official statistics and the registered databases, each cited on its chart.

records.event_context: 2026-2030 LitioMx institutional program published in Diario Oficial
records.summary_en: The 2026-2030 institutional program of LitioMx, published in the official gazette, reaffirms that no concessions or permits will be granted for lithium, that LitioMx controls the value chain, and plans a small industrial battery-pack plant designed by 2029.
records.quote_original: El litio es patrimonio de la Nación y su exploración, explotación, beneficio y aprovechamiento se reserva en favor del pueblo de México
records.quote_en: Lithium is the patrimony of the Nation and its exploration, exploitation, processing and use are reserved for the people of Mexico

source.name: El CEO

records.notes: Reported 27 July 2026; exact DOF publication date not seen.

records.event_context: Mañanera on US-led multilateral critical minerals talks
records.summary_en: Sheinbaum said Mexico's mineral reserves belong to Mexico, their exploitation corresponds to Mexico, and this is not subject to any negotiation; Mexico is ceding nothing.
records.quote_original: Las reservas de minerales son de México. Y en todo caso su explotación le corresponde a México... eso no está a ninguna negociación.
records.quote_en: Mineral reserves belong to Mexico. And in any case their exploitation corresponds to Mexico... that is not under any negotiation.

source.name: Excélsior

records.event_context: Mexico's participation in US-led 60-day multilateral critical minerals talks
records.summary_en: Ebrard said that amid geopolitical competition Mexico must guarantee its own supply of critical minerals it lacks, participating in multilateral talks on the basis of mutual respect, sovereignty and fair access.
records.quote_original: Nosotros tenemos que ocuparnos de garantizar el suministro de minerales críticos para México, porque nos hacen falta muchos minerales
records.quote_en: We have to take care of guaranteeing the supply of critical minerals for Mexico, because we lack many minerals

source.name: La Política Online

records.notes: Talks also involve India and South Korea; China not named by Ebrard.

records.event_context: Mañanera on US critical minerals talks and mining concessions
records.summary_en: Sheinbaum said nothing had been signed with the US on critical minerals, that Mexico would not change its mining law or open new mines as a result, and that over 200 unproductive concessions would return to the state.
records.quote_original: No hay nada firmado… Estados Unidos investiga en su país y nosotros exploramos en el nuestro, cada quien conforme a sus propias leyes
records.quote_en: Nothing is signed... the United States researches in its country and we explore in ours, each according to its own laws

source.name: Diario de Yucatán

records.event_context: Announcement of U.S.-Mexico Action Plan on Critical Minerals
records.summary_en: USTR Greer announced a U.S.-Mexico action plan to develop coordinated trade policies on critical minerals, including possible price floors for imports, within 60 days.
records.quote_original: Today's announcement demonstrates the United States and Mexico's shared commitment to address global market distortions that have left North American critical minerals supply chains vulnerable to disruptions.
records.quote_en: Today's announcement demonstrates the United States and Mexico's shared commitment to address global market distortions that have left North American critical minerals supply chains vulnerable to disruptions.

source.name: USTR

records.notes: Statement does not name China explicitly; 'market distortions' widely read as referring to China.

records.event_context: U.S.-Mexico Action Plan on Critical Minerals
records.summary_en: Ebrard said the Economy Ministry, which oversees the Geological Survey and mining regulation, would form a team to develop a joint work plan with the US on critical minerals, each side respecting its own laws and sovereignty.
records.quote_original: vamos a desarrollar un plan de trabajo conjunto... cada quien, respetando sus normas legales, son diferentes las nuestras a las de ellos. Y respetando cada quien la soberanía del otro
records.quote_en: we are going to develop a joint work plan... each respecting its legal norms, ours differ from theirs, and each respecting the other's sovereignty

source.name: Vanguardia

records.event_context: Planned meetings with USTR Greer on critical minerals and USMCA
records.summary_en: Ebrard announced meetings on 3-4 February with USTR Greer to discuss cooperation on critical minerals such as lithium, copper, nickel, cobalt and graphite, and said the USMCA was not at risk.
records.quote_original: Yo no veo que esté en riesgo el tratado, porque ya estamos en consultas formales los tres países, ya terminamos el proceso de consulta
records.quote_en: I do not see the treaty at risk, because the three countries are already in formal consultations, we have already finished the consultation process

source.name: Uno TV

records.event_context: Mañanera after call with US on USMCA review and critical minerals
records.summary_en: Sheinbaum said critical minerals were being discussed in multilateral settings rather than in her bilateral calls, ahead of the 1 July 2026 USMCA joint review.

source.name: Uno TV

records.event_context: Mañanera on US 50% copper tariff
records.summary_en: Sheinbaum noted Mexico exports more copper to China than to the US, much of the US-bound share being scrap refined there, said a delegation would negotiate in Washington and that Mexico would seek other export options.
records.quote_original: Nuestra responsabilidad es buscar la mejor negociación posible con Estados Unidos y, al mismo tiempo, buscar otras opciones para la producción nacional y la exportación a otros lugares.
records.quote_en: Our responsibility is to seek the best possible negotiation with the United States and, at the same time, seek other options for national production and export to other places.

source.name: Expansión Política

speaker.name: Francisco Cervantes Díaz
speaker.role: President of the Consejo Coordinador Empresarial (CCE)

records.event_context: Business sector reaction to US 50% copper tariff
records.summary_en: The head of Mexico's main business council said the private sector did not understand the reasons for the US copper tariff given that copper is needed and produced in the region, noting Mexico is a top-four world producer.

source.name: Zeta Tijuana

records.notes: Business actor.

records.event_context: Reaction to Trump's announced 50% copper tariff
records.summary_en: Ebrard said Mexico first needed to understand what products the announced US 50% copper tariff would apply to, and planned talks with US officials.
records.quote_original: We need to know what it applies to. We're going to understand that first.
records.quote_en: We need to know what it applies to. We're going to understand that first.

source.name: Mexico News Daily

records.notes: Quote is MND English translation of Spanish original.

records.event_context: Announcement of constitutional reform initiative to dissolve LitioMx
records.summary_en: PAN deputy Sánchez announced an initiative to abolish LitioMx, calling it a bankrupt 'white elephant' with payroll spending but no extraction projects despite a budget increase.
records.quote_original: Hablamos de la manada de elefantes blancos en la granja corrupta de Morena
records.quote_en: We are talking about the herd of white elephants on Morena's corrupt farm

source.name: Quadratín

records.event_context: New national lithium strategy expanding LitioMx
records.summary_en: Sheinbaum announced a broadened role for LitioMx beyond extraction, including research and battery and solar panel manufacturing, with Pemex to create a lithium subsidiary to lead exploration and exploitation.

source.name: Mexico Business News

records.notes: Date approximate (article date).

records.event_context: Plan Sonora progress with US support
records.summary_en: Ebrard said the Economy Ministry was facilitating agreements to speed up Mexico's lithium production on Sheinbaum's instruction, describing Plan Sonora as jointly designed with the United States around electromobility and semiconductors.
records.quote_original: The Ministry of Economy is facilitating the necessary agreements, and President Sheinbaum's directive is to expedite Mexico's lithium production
records.quote_en: The Ministry of Economy is facilitating the necessary agreements, and President Sheinbaum's directive is to expedite Mexico's lithium production

source.name: Mexico Business News

records.notes: Quote is MBN English translation; date approximate (article date).

records.event_context: Analysis of LitioMx 2025 budget
records.summary_en: IMCO's Ocampo said that although LitioMx's proposed 2025 funding rose about 31.6% it remained insufficient to develop lithium projects.

source.name: Mexico Business News

records.notes: Think tank actor; quote attribution in article unclear, so paraphrased.

records.event_context: Mañanera on lithium technology and Plan Sonora
records.summary_en: Sheinbaum said Mexico's lithium has unique characteristics, mainly in Sonora clays, and that the goal is to use domestically developed technology to extract it and keep the whole production chain in Mexico rather than export it.
records.quote_original: Our goal is to implement this technology to extract lithium and establish the entire production chain within Mexico rather than exporting it.
records.quote_en: Our goal is to implement this technology to extract lithium and establish the entire production chain within Mexico rather than exporting it.

source.name: Mexico Business News

records.notes: Quote is MBN English translation of Spanish original; statement date approximate (article date).

records.event_context: Response to Ganfeng ICSID arbitration filing
records.summary_en: AMLO said Mexico would seek a negotiated deal with Ganfeng after its ICSID arbitration claim, while maintaining that the earlier concessions were generic mining concessions not applicable to lithium.
records.quote_original: Sí puede llevarse a cabo alguna asociación, pero con el predominio del interés nacional, en el caso del litio.
records.quote_en: Some association can take place, but with the predominance of the national interest, in the case of lithium.

source.name: Mining.com (Reuters)

records.notes: Quote from Xataka México report of the same mañanera: https://www.xataka.com.mx/automovil/amlo-aclara-litio-concesiones-canceladas-mineral-sera-defendido-china

records.event_context: Response to Ganfeng ICSID claim
records.summary_en: Buenrostro said Ganfeng's arbitration claim lacked merit and Mexico would win, though such cases take many years.
records.quote_original: Nosotros creemos que no tienen elementos. Vamos a ganar
records.quote_en: We believe they have no grounds. We are going to win

source.name: Bloomberg Línea

records.notes: Stance coded toward the Chinese company's claim.

records.event_context: ICSID arbitration filing against Mexico
records.summary_en: Ganfeng and its UK subsidiaries filed an ICSID claim against Mexico over the August 2023 cancellation of nine lithium concessions in Sonora, invoking the Mexico-China and Mexico-UK investment treaties.

source.name: Bloomberg Línea

records.notes: Corporate act; stance fields not applicable.

records.event_context: Ganfeng's Sonora lithium project after concession cancellation
records.summary_en: Secker said Ganfeng had been trying to discuss with the Mexican government how they could work together under commercially viable arrangements, but that no one would invest US$1 billion without security.
records.quote_original: Nadie va a invertir US$ 1,000 millones a menos que tenga algún tipo de seguridad.
records.quote_en: Nobody is going to invest US$1 billion unless they have some kind of security.

source.name: Gestión (Bloomberg)

records.notes: Spanish rendering of an English interview; corporate actor.

records.event_context: Mañanera after Ganfeng disclosed cancellation of its Sonora concessions
records.summary_en: AMLO said lithium concessions were under review because they had originally been granted for gold, silver and copper, not lithium, and that lithium belongs to the nation as a strategic mineral.
records.quote_original: We have decided that lithium belongs to the nation because it's a strategic mineral.
records.quote_en: We have decided that lithium belongs to the nation because it's a strategic mineral.

source.name: Mining.com (Reuters)

records.notes: Quote is Reuters English translation of Spanish original.

records.event_context: Interview on LitioMx plans
records.summary_en: Taddei said existing concessions would be respected, that the state's role vis-a-vis private participation had been misinterpreted, and that his duty was to obtain lithium in the most economically viable way.
records.quote_original: El Estado mexicano, aunque suene trillado, es respetuoso de la ley y eso ha sido una orden del presidente desde el inicio. Se respetarán las concesiones
records.quote_en: The Mexican state, trite as it sounds, respects the law and that has been the president's order from the start. Concessions will be respected

source.name: Expansión

records.notes: Article reports first production expected around 2028.

records.event_context: Promulgation of Mining Law reform in Diario Oficial
records.summary_en: The reform package cutting mining concessions to up to 80 years and water concessions to 30 years was published in the official gazette; AMLO argued it did not harm investors, noting miners had earned record profits.
records.quote_original: han obtenido utilidades y en algunos casos, como nunca
records.quote_en: they have obtained profits, and in some cases like never before

source.name: Zeta Tijuana

records.notes: Quote date approximate (reported with promulgation).

records.event_context: Explaining new Mining Law
records.summary_en: Buenrostro said that under the new law concessions in water-scarce areas would only be granted with presidential authorization and that there would be no new concessions because people have priority over water.
records.quote_original: No habrá concesiones nuevas porque no hay agua y la prioridad la tiene la gente
records.quote_en: There will be no new concessions because there is no water and people have priority

source.name: El Financiero

records.notes: Exact date of remark approximate (article date).

records.event_context: Mañanera after Congress approved 2023 Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: AMLO said the newly approved Mining Law would apply to future concessions and that his government would not grant any new concessions, recalling environmental damage from gold mining at Cerro de San Pedro.
records.quote_original: una ley para aplicarse en el futuro cuando se entreguen concesiones, si es que van a entregar concesiones, en el caso de nosotros no vamos a entregar concesiones
records.quote_en: a law to be applied in the future when concessions are granted, if they are granted; in our case we will not grant concessions

source.name: N+

records.event_context: Guerrero state congress session commenting on federal Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: In the Guerrero state congress, Guevara praised the federal mining reform as putting citizens, environment and national territory at the centre and respecting natural resources and communities.
records.quote_original: Hoy estamos ante una reforma que representa el respeto a nuestros recursos naturales y a la población de las comunidades
records.quote_en: Today we are facing a reform that represents respect for our natural resources and for the population of the communities

source.name: Congreso del Estado de Guerrero

records.notes: Party affiliation inferred from content of the intervention; verify.

records.event_context: Senate vote on 2023 Mining Law and water concessions reform
records.summary_en: The Senate approved the Mining Law, National Waters Law and environmental law reforms with 66 votes in a session held at an alternate venue without the opposition, sending them to the executive.

source.name: Bloomberg Línea

records.notes: Session ran late 28 April into 29 April; date of report used.

speaker.name: Grupo México (Leonardo Contreras)
speaker.role: Director of Administration and Finance, Mining Division, Grupo México

records.event_context: Analyst/investor call during Senate debate on Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: A Grupo México executive told analysts the company saw no effect of the proposed Mining Law reform on its current business and was awaiting the outcome.
records.quote_original: No vemos ningún efecto en nuestro negocio actual, estamos esperando las resoluciones
records.quote_en: We see no effect on our current business, we are waiting for the resolutions

source.name: Bloomberg (via Cámara de Diputados síntesis)

records.notes: Corporate actor.

records.event_context: Press release on Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: COPARMEX asked the Senate not to fast-track the mining reform, calling for an open parliament with experts and firms, investment certainty, and postponing approval until September.
records.quote_original: es necesario escuchar a expertos y a las empresas mediante un parlamento abierto
records.quote_en: it is necessary to listen to experts and companies through an open parliament

source.name: COPARMEX

records.notes: Business association, not government.

speaker.name: Asociación de Ingenieros de Minas, Metalurgistas y Geólogos de México (AIMMGM)

records.event_context: Reaction to Chamber approval of Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: The mining engineers' association urged the Senate to hold an open parliament before ratifying the fast-tracked reform, warning of provisions on exploration, payments and restrictions affecting the industry.
records.quote_original: Antes de ratificar la reforma aprobada por la Cámara de Diputados, el Senado de la República debe convocar a un parlamento abierto
records.quote_en: Before ratifying the reform approved by the Chamber of Deputies, the Senate must convene an open parliament

source.name: Forbes México (via Cámara de Diputados síntesis)

records.notes: Industry actor.

records.event_context: Vote on 2023 Mining Law and water concessions reform
records.summary_en: The Chamber of Deputies approved in general the AMLO-backed reform of the Mining Law, National Waters Law and environmental laws by 290 votes to 186 with 1 abstention; Morena, PT, PVEM and MC supported it while PAN, PRI and PRD opposed.

source.name: Excélsior

records.notes: In particular: 251-209-1 (Infobae via Cámara síntesis).

records.event_context: Chamber of Deputies debate on 2023 Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: Former economy minister Guajardo opposed the reform, arguing that articles 10 and 10 bis would cause Mexican mining to lose its potential.
records.quote_original: con los artículos 10 y 10 bis de la reforma, la minería mexicana perderá su potencial
records.quote_en: with articles 10 and 10 bis of the reform, Mexican mining will lose its potential

source.name: Excélsior

records.notes: Debate ran overnight 20-21 April 2023.

speaker.name: Manuel Rodríguez González
speaker.role: Federal Deputy (Morena); President of the Energy Commission

records.event_context: Chamber of Deputies debate on 2023 Mining Law and water concessions reform
records.summary_en: Presenting the reform, Rodríguez said its central aim was to recover state stewardship over mineral and water resources; the bill shortened mining concessions and water concessions for mining.
records.quote_original: La esencia y objetivo central es recuperar la rectoría del Estado sobre los recursos minerales e hídricos del subsuelo mexicano
records.quote_en: The essence and central objective is to recover the State's stewardship over the mineral and water resources of the Mexican subsoil

source.name: Zeta Tijuana

records.notes: Debate ran overnight 20-21 April 2023.

records.event_context: Signing of lithium nationalization decree, Bacadéhuachi, Sonora
records.summary_en: In Bacadéhuachi, Sonora, AMLO signed a decree transferring lithium reserve areas to the Energy Ministry, saying lithium would be nationalized so that foreigners from Russia, China or the US could not exploit it.
records.quote_original: Vamos a nacionalizar el litio para que no lo puedan explotar los extranjeros ni de Rusia, ni de China, ni de Estados Unidos
records.quote_en: We are going to nationalize lithium so that foreigners from Russia, China or the United States cannot exploit it

source.name: N+

records.notes: Stance toward CHN/USA coded negative regarding their exploitation of Mexican lithium.

speaker.name: Alfonso Durazo
speaker.role: Governor of Sonora; coordinator of Litio para México

records.event_context: Appointment as coordinator of LitioMx
records.summary_en: Durazo said that if lithium exploitation becomes a profitable business its benefits must be shared with local people, and that the Sonora government would hold a stake in LitioMx.
records.quote_original: esos beneficios tienen que ser compartidos con la gente local, si no, para mí francamente no tendría ningún sentido
records.quote_en: those benefits have to be shared with local people; otherwise, frankly, it would make no sense to me

source.name: Expansión Política

records.event_context: Senate debate on lithium Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: Morena senator Armenta defended the reform, arguing that the private sector would still participate since the state company would sell lithium to private firms.
records.quote_original: Se lo vende a los particulares
records.quote_en: It is sold to private parties

source.name: Expansión Política

records.event_context: Senate debate on lithium Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: PAN senator Damián Zepeda opposed the lithium reform, arguing the government should not act as a businessman in lithium exploitation.
records.quote_original: el gobierno es pésimo para ser empresario
records.quote_en: the government is terrible at being a businessman

source.name: Expansión Política

records.event_context: Senate debate on lithium Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: Bermúdez criticized the reform for lacking precision on which minerals would be considered 'strategic'.

source.name: Expansión Política

records.event_context: Senate vote on lithium Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: The Senate approved in general the Mining Law reform reserving lithium exploration and exploitation to the state, by 87 votes to 20 with 16 abstentions.

records.event_context: Mañanera after failure of constitutional electricity reform; call to pass Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: AMLO urged legislators to approve his Mining Law reform nationalizing lithium, saying it should be used only for national development and that a state company would explore, extract, process and sell it.
records.quote_original: nacionalicemos el litio. Así de claro, que solo se utilice para el beneficio del desarrollo nacional.
records.quote_en: let's nationalize lithium. That clear, so that it is only used for the benefit of national development.

source.name: El Financiero

records.event_context: Vote on Mining Law reform declaring lithium of public utility
records.summary_en: The Chamber of Deputies approved in general the reform to the Mining Law nationalizing lithium by 298 votes in favour and 197 abstentions; PAN and PRI deputies abstained, while Movimiento Ciudadano voted against parts of it.

source.name: Expansión Política

records.notes: In particular: 275 for, 187 abstentions, 24 against (MC).

records.event_context: Chamber of Deputies debate on lithium Mining Law reform
records.summary_en: Chertorivski argued that lithium concessions could not be prohibited by ordinary statute and that it had to be done through the Constitution.
records.quote_original: No se puede prohibir en una ley una concesión, se tiene que hacer desde la Constitución
records.quote_en: A concession cannot be prohibited in a law, it has to be done from the Constitution

source.name: Expansión Política

records.summary_en: AMLO said existing mining concessions did not cover lithium, which he called a strategic mineral belonging to the nation, and that the state would exploit it; he said Mexico did not want to be a territory of conflict between Russia, China or the US.
records.quote_original: el litio lo va a explotar la nación. El litio ya, para que se entienda bien, no es ni siquiera del Gobierno o del Estado, el litio es del pueblo
records.quote_en: lithium will be exploited by the nation. Lithium, to be clear, does not even belong to the government or the state, lithium belongs to the people
